records.title: Radio-frequency reflectometry in silicon carbide large-area transistors
records.abstract: Radio-frequency (RF) reflectometry is widely used for high-bandwidth readout of semiconductor quantum devices at cryogenic temperatures, but its application has mainly been limited to nanoscale structures with relatively small capacitances. Here, we investigate RF readout in a different regime by applying gate-based reflectometry to a large-area silicon carbide transistor with parasitic capacitances orders of magnitude larger than those of typical quantum devices, conditions normally expected to hinder RF readout. We observe a gate-dependent RF response which degrades and eventually becomes unresolved as temperature is lowered, although DC transport measurements continue to provide evidence of channel formation down to deep cryogenic temperatures. We attribute this behavior to impedance changes introduced by carrier freeze-out in the transistor drift region, and examine a modified circuit configuration designed to recover sensitivity to changes in channel resistance under these conditions. These results establish how parasitic pathways and device geometry can limit RF readout, providing insight into the design of scalable cryogenic-CMOS quantum systems.

records.title: Loss Characteristics and Optimization of a High-Power IGBT Phase-Shifted Full-Bridge ZVS Primary Inverter for Electric-Vehicle Wireless Charging
records.abstract: Buried wireless charging electric-vehicle inverter needs to achieve ZVS in face of adverse factors such as offset of primary inverter, variations of primary and mutual inductance, and variations in loading conditions. In this paper, analysis on the effects of a 10 kW IGBT phase-shifted full-bridge inverter with series-series resonant link on buried electric-vehicle wireless charging will be conducted. The loss model for the IGBT inverter, which integrates IGBT turn-off tail energy dissipation, partial ZVS operations, diode freewheeling, dead-time circulation and material losses of coil, ferrite and shielding materials, can be built based on publicly available datasheet and prototype specifications. Afterward, a segmented floating frequency phase-shift controller is employed to compensate for the drifting of resonant frequency and maintain ZVS operations with L_p-M mismatch. The performance of the proposed approach is evaluated through publicly available parameter simulation, benchmark analysis and controller logic CIL validation. The proposed approach increases the simulated ZVS coverage from 62% to 90%, cuts down the total rated losses by 17.0%, improves the peak efficiency to 94.7% and reduces the predicted maximum junction temperature by about 17°C.

records.title: Super-Junction Insulated-Gate Bipolar Transistor with a Vertical Channel Arrangement and a Shielded Floating Charge-Carrier Accumulation Layer
records.abstract: A device structure for a superjunction insulated-gate bipolar transistor featuring a floating charge-carrier accumulation layer has been proposed and investigated via computer simulation. In this structure, the accumulation layer is shielded by an underlying p -type layer. It is established that the charge-carrier concentration within the accumulation layer does not affect the breakdown voltage. Furthermore, the proposed insulated-gate bipolar transistor structure demonstrates superior efficiency compared to conventional superjunction trench insulated-gate bipolar transistor’s, as well as those utilizing a floating p -region or an adaptive holeextraction path. Specifically, at an identical on-state voltage drop of 0.946 V, the turn-off energy loss of the proposed device is 75.38 % lower than that of a superjunction trench insulated-gate bipolar transistor with a floating p -region, and 52 % lower than that of a device with an adaptive hole-extraction path. Conversely, for a constant turn-off energy loss of 2.3 mJ/cm 2 , the on-state voltage drop of the proposed device is 39.86 % lower than that of a standard superjunction trench insulated-gate bipolar transistor.

records.title: Threshold voltage engineering via diode-embedded p-GaN gate HEMTs
records.abstract: In this work, enhancement-mode (E-mode) p-GaN/AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) with monolithically embedded gate diodes are investigated to explore the use of embedded diode width as a design parameter for threshold-voltage engineering. The embedded diode geometry modulates the electrostatic potential within the gate stack, thereby tuning the threshold voltage. A wide threshold-voltage tuning range of 1.45–3.3 V was achieved, where 1.45 V corresponds to the reference device without an embedded diode and 3.3 V corresponds to the device with a diode-to-HEMT channel ratio of 0.1. In addition, the diode-embedded structure exhibits improved forward gate breakdown voltage while maintaining comparable on-resistance and off-state breakdown voltage. Pulsed bias measurements reveal that smaller diode widths effectively suppress negative threshold-voltage shifts, indicating enhanced dynamic gate stability. These results demonstrate that monolithically embedded gate diodes provide an effective and scalable approach for threshold-voltage engineering and reliability enhancement in E-mode GaN HEMTs for power-switching applications.

records.title: Negative Activation Energy Under Dynamic Stress of 650 V E-mode GaN HEMTs
records.abstract: We demonstrate for the first time that the process responsible for dynamic R ON degradation in GaN HEMTs operated under application-close SALT hard-switching (HS) conditions exhibits a negative activation energy. This behavior has been attributed to the mitigation of hot-electron-induced degradation at higher temperatures, resulting from the reduced electron mean free path. In addition, a novel real-time in-situ technique to monitor the threshold voltage (V TH ) variation during HS operation is presented. Negligible V TH variation was observed during the tests, along with a significant increase in on-resistance: this result supports the conclusion that hot-electron trapping in the access region is the dominant mechanism responsible for the observed degradation.

records.title: Threshold voltage instability in Schottky p-GaN gate HEMTs under dynamic gate stress
records.abstract: This work investigates the threshold voltage instability of 650-V Schottky p-GaN gate HEMTs under dynamic gate stress (DGS). The effects of gate bias, temperature, switching frequency, and duty cycle on the threshold voltage shift (ΔV TH ) are experimentally analyzed. The results show that ΔV TH strongly depends on the applied stress conditions and arises from the interplay of multiple charge-trapping mechanisms within the gate stack. In particular, increasing gate bias enhances the negative threshold voltage shift, while higher temperature and switching frequency promote positive contributions that partially compensate for the negative drift. Duty cycle is also found to play a key role by modifying the effective positive-bias time and the balance between competing trapping mechanisms. A comparison with DC constant-voltage stress further highlights the importance of dynamic stress conditions in determining the threshold-voltage evolution. These findings provide further insight into the reliability behavior of p-GaN HEMTs under DGS conditions relevant to switching operation.

records.title: TD-MSEFormer: temporal dependency multi-scale expert former for IGBT remaining useful life prediction
records.abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of insulated gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs) is important for ensuring the reliability of power electronic systems. However, IGBT degradation sequences usually exhibit nonlinear evolution, mixed short-term and long-term dependencies, and stage-dependent degradation characteristics, which makes robust RUL prediction challenging. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Temporal Dependency Multi-Scale Expert Former (TD-MSEFormer). Specifically, a Sequential Dependency Calibration Module (SDCM) is introduced to enhance degradation-related temporal dependency representation. A Multi-Scale Temporal Expert Block (MSTEB) is designed to capture degradation patterns at different temporal scales, while a Temporal Dual-Attention (TDA) block further refines local temporal interactions. Extensive experiments on NASA IGBT Aging Dataset demonstrate that the proposed TD-MSEFormer consistently outperforms other methods, achieving the best overall RUL prediction performance with superior accuracy, robust generalization, and stable degradation representation under complex nonlinear aging conditions.

records.title: Low-loss superjunction SiC MOSFET with improved breakdown voltage and reverse-recovery performance
records.abstract: Conventional silicon carbide (SiC) trench metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) still face challenges such as high body diode forward voltage, and difficulty in balancing static and dynamic performance. To address these issues, a novel split-gate multi-channel superjunction SiC MOSFET with an integrated metal-oxide-semiconductor-channel diode, named as MSM-MOS, is proposed. The electrical characteristics of the proposed device are investigated using technology computer-aided design simulations and compared with those of a conventional trench MOSFET and a superjunction MOSFET with an integrated Schottky barrier diode. The MSM-MOS achieves a breakdown voltage of 2037 V and a specific on-resistance of 0.70 mΩ·cm 2 , showing improved drain-to-source blocking capability in the off-state and on-state conduction performance. In reverse conduction, the MSM-MOS shows a forward voltage of 1.77 V and a low reverse-recovery charge. Consequently, the MSM-MOS achieves the highest Baliga figure of merit of 5.92 GW cm −2 and the lowest dynamic figure of merit of 32.9 mΩ·nC among the three device structures.

records.title: Physical origin and mitigation of output-capacitance hysteresis in superjunction devices
records.abstract: The output-capacitance hysteresis of charge-balanced vertical drift regions, commonly referred to as superjunctions (SJs), has attracted renewed attention because of its impact on switching losses in resonant and soft-switching power converters. Previous studies have linked this behaviour to stranded charge in the p/n semiconductor pillars and to the finite carrier velocity required for charge redistribution during voltage transients. In this work, the physical origin of this hysteresis is revisited by analysing the charge dynamics during charging and discharging. Finite-element simulations are used to assess the influence of charge-balance condition, temperature, partial dopant ionisation, cell pitch, voltage slew rate, and non-uniform doping, including graded pillar profiles. The results indicate that capacitance hysteresis is strongly governed by field-dependent carrier transport at the boundaries of the depletion regions, which controls the rate at which mobile carriers can be removed from, or replenished within, the charge-balanced structure. Based on these findings, design guidelines are proposed that reduce hysteresis-related energy loss by approximately 30% compared with a uniformly doped reference SJ structure, while preserving a favourable specific on-state resistance, R on , sp , and without substantially increasing process complexity.

records.title: Physics-based gate stack optimization of p-GaN/AlGaN/GaN HEMTs for balanced threshold voltage and on-resistance
records.abstract: In this article, the gate-stack design space of p-GaN/AlGaN/GaN HEMTs (high electron mobility transistors) is explored to achieve a balanced threshold voltage ( V T ) and on-resistance ( R on ). Physics-based analytical models for V T and R on are validated against experimental data and subsequently employed for a 10,000-point design-space exploration encompassing variations in p-GaN doping concentration, Schottky built-in potential, AlGaN thickness, and Al mole fraction. While a high V T is essential for robust enhancement-mode operation and adequate gate-noise immunity, a low R on is required to minimize conduction losses. The study reveals the inherent trade-off between V T and R on , and identifies an optimum gate-stack design region that balances these competing requirements. Based on the explored design space, practical design guidelines are established to maintain V T within the range of 1.7–2.2 V while achieving the lowest possible R on under process-induced variations of gate-stack parameters.

records.title: Beyond Passive Reliability: Repeated Electron Wind Force Rejuvenation of GaN HEMTs
records.abstract: Performance degradation in electronic devices is caused by nucleation and accumulation of electrically active defects and traps. This spotlight on applications introduces a novel paradigm to actively reverse the damage process with electron wind force (EWF). EWF is a nonintrusive and nonequilibrium mechanism for defect migration at near-ambient average temperatures. Enhancement-mode gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) were systematically degraded via high-temperature storage at 310 °C, which induced upto 13% reduction in drain current, 0.2 V negative threshold voltage shift, and 12% reduction in peak transconductance. A brief 1-minute application of EWF achieved full parameter recovery. Crucially, across five consecutive degradation-rejuvenation cycles, the HEMTs maintained excellent resilience, retaining 98.5% of their initial drain current, 97% of peak transconductance, 95% of gate-lag, and 93% of drain-lag responses. These findings indicate that periodic in operando EWF rejuvenation may realize unprecedented reliability of wide-bandgap electronics in mission-critical operations.

records.title: Optimizing gate voltage of SiC MOSFETs to enhance the lifetime and reliability of an H-ANPC inverter
records.abstract: SiC MOSFETs offer significant advantages over their silicon counterparts, including higher breakdown voltage, faster switching speed, and better thermal conductivity, making them well-suited for high-frequency, high-voltage, and high-temperature applications in power electronics. Nevertheless, the long-term reliability of SiC MOSFETs remains a major challenge, as device failures can lead to system-level malfunctions, unplanned outages, and elevated safety risks, particularly in mission-critical applications. To assess their reliability under typical converter stresses, a hybrid-active neutral point clamped (H-ANPC) inverter is used. This article proposed an active gate voltage control (AGVC) technique, which is used to develop a scheme for optimizing gate voltage to improve the reliability and lifetime of SiC MOSFETs within the H-ANPC inverter. The article includes detailed explanations of the experimental setups for IAT, TDDB, and the H-ANPC inverter, along with an analysis of the results and lifetime modeling. records.title: Research on the Short-Term Overcurrent Failure Mechanism of Press-Pack IGBT Devices Under MMC Conditions
records.abstract: With the rapid deployment of flexible high-voltage direct-current (HVDC) systems, high-power press-pack insulated-gate bipolar transistors (PP-IGBTs) have become critical components. However, field data indicate premature overcurrent failures in PP-IGBTs under modular multilevel converter (MMC) operations. This study systematically investigates the short-term overcurrent failure mechanisms of PP-IGBTs under MMC-specific operational stresses, distinguishing them from conventional short-circuit or avalanche modes. A power cycling test platform emulating MMC submodule conditions was developed to capture the evolution of terminal characteristics. Furthermore, a double-pulse test platform was established to reproduce failure locations under service-relevant stresses. The study reveals a distinctive failure mode characterized by pronounced gate leakage and the eventual loss of normal gate control, leading to functional open-circuit failure—a phenomenon that has been rarely reported in the existing MMC literature. The experimental results indicate a decreasing trend in short-term overcurrent withstand capability with increasing clamping force and reveal a preliminary relationship between peak current and measured emitter-side temperature at failure. These findings provide insights into the failure mechanisms of PP-IGBTs and offer practical guidance for device selection, converter design, and reliability assessment.

records.title: High frequency performance of GaN HEMT with thin InAlGaN barrier
records.abstract: In this study, the optimization of the InAlGaN/GaN heterostructure and the fabrication of RF high-electron-mobility-transistors (HEMTs) on a SiC substrate are reported. Owing to the outstanding 2DEG properties of the InAlGaN/GaN heterostructure, the InAlGaN/GaN HEMT achieved a high on-current of 1280 mA/mm and a transconductance of 482.8 mS/mm with a low off-state leakage current of 5 × 10−4 A/mm. Furthermore, the InAlGaN/GaN HEMT exhibited a high fT/fmax of 93/154 GHz and a breakdown voltage of 56 V, resulting in a Johnson’s figure of merit value of 5.2 THz V. These distinguished characteristics of the device demonstrate that the InAlGaN/GaN heterostructure is a promising candidate for high power and high frequency applications.

records.title: Optimized narrow mesa superjunction trench insulated gate bipolar transistor with shallow emitter trench-controlled P-column
records.abstract: This paper proposes and investigates a novel narrow mesa (NM) superjunction trench insulated gate bipolar transistor (SJ-TIGBT) featuring a shallow emitter trench-controlled P-column (STCP). The formed NM and STCP structures not only enhance the carrier storage effect and reduce on-state voltage drop ( V CEON ) in the on-state, but also accelerate the extraction of excess holes during turn-off and suppress displacement current during turn-on. Thus, improved performance is achieved for the proposed device. Furthermore, a split gate (SG) is incorporated into the gate trench of the proposed device to shield the negative impact on it of the dummy P-type region, which further reduces the electromagnetic interference noise. Simulation results show that compared with a conventional SJ-TIGBT, the proposed STCP-SJ-TIGBT achieves a 41% lower V CEON at a collector-current density of 200 A cm −2 and a 72.3% lower turn-off loss ( E OFF ) at a V CEON of 1.37 V. The turn-on d I C /d t of the STCP-SJ-TIGBT at the same gate resistance and the reverse recovery d V AK /d t of the freewheeling diode at the same turn-on loss are reduced by 79.1% and 24.4%, respectively. Moreover, introduction of a SG reduces the Miller capacitance of the proposed device by 94.1%, further improving its E ON –d V KA /d t trade-off at negligible cost to V CEON and E OFF .

records.title: Characterization and inversion of continuous EMVP signals under PWM excitation in IGBT devices
records.abstract: Electromagnetic vibration pulse based condition monitoring has shown considerable potential for power electronic devices. Existing studies mainly rely on single turn-on or turn-off electromagnetic vibration pulse signals extracted from double-pulse tests, which are not fully representative of practical converter operation under pulse width modulation. In this paper, continuous electromagnetic vibration pulse signals excited by multi-cycle switching in TO-247 packaged IGBT devices are investigated through theoretical analysis and experiments. The time- and frequency-domain characteristics under different switching periods and duty cycles are analyzed, revealing spectral and modal features specific to multi-cycle excitation. A regularization-enhanced cycle-stacking inversion method is proposed to reconstruct single-cycle signals from multi-cycle responses, and two indicators, R qs and R m , are introduced to evaluate inversion feasibility. Simulation and experimental results show that reliable inversion is achieved only when inter-cycle interaction is sufficiently weak. This study represents a first essential step toward electromagnetic voiceprint (EMVP)-based degradation assessment under practical PWM operation by establishing the feasibility and limitations of extracting single-cycle features from continuous signals. The findings provide a methodological basis for subsequent fault diagnosis and degradation evaluation of IGBT devices using EMVP features reconstructed from continuous operating signals.

records.title: Ultrawide-bandgap semiconductors beyond SiC and GaN: A multidimensional framework for the emerging fourth generation
records.abstract: The evolution of semiconductor technologies is better understood as an application-driven expansion of accessible operating space than as a monotonic increase in bandgap. Silicon established scalable integrated electronics, III-V compounds enabled direct-bandgap optoelectronics and high-mobility radio-frequency (RF) devices, and SiC and GaN extended semiconductor operation toward high-field, high-temperature and high-efficiency power and RF systems. Emerging applications increasingly demand combinations of higher critical fields, thermal robustness, deep-ultraviolet functionality, extreme-environment tolerance and scalable manufacturability that push beyond conventional wide-bandgap platforms. Here, we develop a multidimensional working framework for the emerging fourth-generation ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) semiconductor landscape, in which bandgap serves as a scope-defining material parameter rather than the sole driver of technological evolution. Diamond, β-Ga 2 O 3 and AlN or Al-rich nitrides are evaluated as complementary platforms in terms of intrinsic material limits, crystal and epitaxial manufacturability, doping and contacts, thermal and interface constraints, reliability and device opportunities. Diamond is further examined as an extended case study to illustrate how wafer scaling, defect control, doping and heterogeneous integration determine whether exceptional intrinsic properties can be translated into manufacturable power, thermal-management and quantum technologies. This framework emphasizes that practical semiconductor performance is governed by coupled material, interface, device and system-level constraints rather than by bandgap alone.

records.title: Simulation study of void impact in trench-filling-epitaxy-based 4H-SiC semi-superjunction schottky rectifiers
records.abstract: This paper establishes an experiment-informed defect-aware TCAD- Response Surface (RS) framework to investigate how trench-filling voids affect the conduction-breakdown trade-off and doping window of 4H-SiC Semi-SuperJunction (SSJ) Schottky rectifiers. Two practical design routes are compared: a void-free route using wide, tilted trenches and a void-included route using narrow, near-vertical trenches. Realistic void configurations derived from experiments are embedded into TCAD for both p-type trench-filling (PTF) and n-type trench-filling (NTF) architectures across varied trench angles and widths. Results show that voids consistently reduce breakdown voltage (BV) while broadening the refill doping window. However, PTF and NTF structures exhibit different void tolerance for varied geometries. In PTF devices, BV degradation is severe in narrow trenches, reaching 146 V, 137 V and 254 V at 2°, 5° and 8°, respectively, but is much smaller in wide trenches, with losses of 15 V at 2° and 12 V at 5°, while void-free refill is achieved at 8°. In NTF devices, where the void lies inside the N-pillar, narrow trenches suffer stronger degradation, with BV losses of 204 and 177 V and R on,sp increases of 25% and 22% at 2° and 5°, respectively. Wide-trench NTF devices still show BV losses of 156 V and 9 V, with 9% and 4% R on,sp penalties. TCAD-RS-based re-optimization is used and shows that narrow PTF structures favor near-vertical sidewalls, whereas wide PTF structures should prioritize void-free filling. NTF structures should always pursue void-free refill through wide, tilted trench designs.

records.title: Defect Engineering in Gallium Nitride Semiconductors for Improving Carrier Mobility and High-Power Electronic Device Reliability
records.source: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews
records.abstract: Gallium nitride power devices increasingly operate at electric-field, switching-frequency, and junction-temperature regimes where defect-mediated carrier trapping becomes a principal constraint on transport stability and operational lifetime. This study investigates how targeted defect engineering can modify the relationship between GaN microstructure, electron mobility, and degradation in high-power electronic devices. The analysis focuses on nitrogen vacancies, gallium vacancies, carbon- and oxygen-related impurities, threading dislocations, and interface traps whose electronic states promote Coulomb scattering, carrier capture, dynamic on-resistance, leakage, and threshold-voltage instability. A defect–transport–reliability framework is developed to connect defect concentration and trap energetics with mobility degradation and electrically activated failure mechanisms. Engineering interventions including epitaxial growth-condition control, compensation management, dislocation reduction, interface passivation, and post-growth thermal processing are comparatively examined. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing defects that primarily limit channel transport from deep-level traps activated under high-field and high-temperature stress. The framework establishes measurable links among trap density, electron mobility, current collapse, leakage evolution, and device degradation, providing a pathway for optimizing GaN heterostructures for sustained high-voltage operation without sacrificing transport performance or switching efficiency.

records.title: Current Status of Research on High‐Electron‐Mobility Transistor Devices on Gallium Nitride and Aluminum Nitride Substrates
records.abstract: Gallium nitride‐based high‐electron‐mobility transistors (GaN HEMTs) are widely used in fields such as microwave communications and power electronics due to their excellent properties, including a wide bandgap, high critical breakdown field strength, and high electron mobility. Although commercial GaN HEMTs on foreign substrates (Si, SiC, and sapphire) are widely adopted, unavoidable heteroepitaxial mismatches in lattice and thermal expansion introduce high dislocation densities, exacerbating current collapse and leakage. This paper systematically reviews the material properties and structural advantages of free‐standing GaN and AlN single‐crystal substrates, detailing the latest research progress on GaN‐substrate HEMTs in terms of substrate doping engineering, buffer layer optimization, and enhancement‐mode device design. The key technological breakthroughs of AlN‐substrate HEMTs in GaN and high‐Al‐content AlGaN channel devices were also explored. It compares the application potential and core challenges of these two technical routes, outlines future development directions, and provides a systematic reference for the research and development of GaN‐based power and RF devices.

records.title: Modeling and Sensitivity Analysis of GaN HEMT Biosensor
records.abstract: Gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) biosensors have recently emerged as promising platforms for highly sensitive and label-free detection of biomolecules. Their exceptional electrical properties, including high carrier mobility, together with the wide bandgap and strong chemical bonds of GaN materials, provide excellent stability under high temperatures, ionizing radiation, and chemically harsh environments. Despite significant experimental progress, comprehensive analytical models capable of linking biomolecular recognition events to the electrical response of GaN biosensors remain limited. This work presents a physics-based, design-oriented analytical modeling framework for AlGaN/GaN HEMT biosensors. The model incorporates biomolecular binding kinetics, the dielectric properties of the hybrid system, and electrostatic coupling to the transistor channel conductivity. Numerical simulations are performed using COMSOL Multiphysics to validate the analytical model. The developed framework provides physical insight into the mechanisms governing biosensor operation and offers practical guidelines for the optimization and comparative assessment of HEMT/MIS-HEMT biosensor architectures.

records.title: A case study on CFD uncertainty and geometric optimization of IGBT liquid cooling plates for high-speed trains
records.abstract: Effective thermal management of insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) modules is essential for the reliable operation of high-speed train power systems. This study presents a computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-based case study of the thermal-hydraulic performance and geometric optimization of an IGBT liquid cooling plate. A multi-factor uncertainty analysis is first conducted to evaluate the effects of numerical settings and establish a reliable simulation framework. The results indicate that turbulence-model selection has a greater influence on the predicted results than mesh resolution and numerical schemes within the investigated orthogonal design. Based on the validated model, the effects of channel geometry are systematically investigated in terms of cross-sectional shape, channel number, and aspect ratio. Among the tested configurations, the rectangular channel provides the best overall balance between heat transfer and pressure loss. An optimal channel-number range of 21-29 is identified, while an aspect ratio of approximately 7.9-9 provides the most favorable thermal-hydraulic performance among the investigated cases. These findings provide design guidance for the IGBT liquid cooling plate considered in this study.

records.title: Multiple-channel AlScN/GaN field-effect transistors
records.abstract: Multiple-channel field-effect transistors based on aluminum scandium nitride (AlScN)/gallium nitride (GaN) heterostructures stand as a promising avenue for next-generation high-frequency applications. In this work, we demonstrate prototype AlScN/GaN super-lattice castellated field-effect transistors (SLCFETs) employing three-channel heterostructures grown by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) and report their direct-current (DC) and small-signal radio-frequency (RF) characteristics. Normalized by active channel width, peak on-current of 3.83 A mm − 1 , cut-off frequency ( f T ) of 31.2 GHz and maximum oscillation frequency ( f MAX ) of 17.7 GHz are measured. These results establish AlScN/GaN SLCFETs as a viable platform for next-generation RF devices, motivating further optimization of substrate and epitaxial growth strategies.

records.title: Gate transport mechanism and PBTI in E-mode GaN HEMT with a p - i - n junction gate
records.abstract: In this Letter, the gate transport mechanism and the positive bias temperature instability in an E-mode GaN high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) with a p-i-n junction gate are investigated. The fabricated device demonstrates remarkable normally off characteristics with a high threshold voltage of 2.8 V at room temperature. Comprehensive electrical characterization identifies Poole–Frenkel emission as the dominant gate conduction mechanism, with potential barrier heights of 0.45 and 0.47 eV extracted from temperature-dependent gate leakage. Capacitance-based deep-level transient spectroscopy reveals two distinct trap states in the p-GaN layer located at 0.54 and 0.88 eV above the valence band, respectively. The positive bias temperature instability characteristics and their underlying mechanisms are also analyzed. This study reveals the material–electrical correlation mechanism in p-i-n junction gate HEMTs, providing a theoretical foundation for the further design of highly reliable p-GaN HEMTs.

records.title: Polarization engineered AlPN barriers for suppression of current collapse in p-GaN gate GaN HEMTs
records.abstract: Current collapse remains a major reliability and performance challenge in GaN based high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs), primarily attributed to trap charging induced by high electric fields near the gate drain region. In this work, the suppression mechanism of current collapse in polarization engineered p-GaN gate AlPN/GaN HEMTs is systematically investigated and benchmarked against conventional p-GaN gate AlGaN/GaN HEMTs using pulsed I-V simulations supported by physics based TCAD analysis. The incorporation of an AlPN barrier enables effective redistribution of the electric field, significantly reducing the peak vertical electric field at the gate drain edge under high voltage stress. Post-stress electron concentration analysis reveals that the AlPN based device exhibits strong electrostatic control, leading to a sharply confined depletion region beneath the gate with minimal extension into the access region. In contrast, the AlGaN based device shows a broader depletion region extending toward the drain access region, resulting in increased access resistance and aggravated current collapse. Quantitatively, the AlGaN/GaN HEMT exhibits a current collapse of 39.3%, whereas the AlPN/GaN HEMT shows a significantly reduced collapse of 6.8% at a drain voltage of 20 V. Correspondingly, the dynamic ON resistance (R ON ) is reduced from 975 Ω to 76 Ω. These results demonstrate that polarization engineered AlPN barriers effectively suppress trap-assisted degradation by mitigating electric field crowding and limiting charge trapping. The proposed AlPN/GaN HEMT architecture therefore presents a promising pathway for high efficiency power switching applications.

records.source: ECS Journal of Solid State Science and Technology
records.abstract: Low-voltage lateral trench split gate tri-gate MOSFETs (SGT-MOSFET) in 4H-SiC are proposed, fabricated, and investigated in this paper, comparing their performance with that of planar gate MOSFETs (PG-MOSFET). The tri-gate MOSFET features top channels on the (0001) face and additional sidewall channels on the (11–20) face, resulting in an increased effective channel width and higher electron mobility. The SGT-MOSFET exhibits drain currents 2.7 and 2.6 times higher than the PG-MOSFET at 25 °C and 200 °C, respectively. The gate oxide reliability is also examined preliminarily. These results highlight the potential of 4H-SiC tri-gate MOSFETs for low-voltage logic circuits and provide a basis for subsequent monolithic integration.

records.title: Study of n-Channel 4H-SiC MOSFETs with a High-k/SiO2 Stacked Gate Dielectric and a p+-Polysilicon Gate
records.abstract: In this study, n-channel 4H-SiC MOSFETs with a high-k/SiO2 stacked gate dielectric and a p+-polysilicon gate are proposed and investigated via numerical simulations. The high-k dielectric increases the gate capacitance, thereby reducing the specific on-state resistance of the devices. The p+-polysilicon increases the work-function difference between the gate and the surface p-SiC, which compensates for the threshold voltage reduction caused by the high-k dielectric. Simulation results demonstrate that replacing the SiO2 and n+-polysilicon with an Al2O3/SiO2 stack and p+-polysilicon, respectively, reduces the specific on-resistance by 26.9% while lowering the threshold voltage by only 0.02 V at 25 °C. At 175 °C, the threshold voltage increases by 0.28 V. The temperature coefficient of the threshold voltage is reduced from −6.2 mV/°C to −4.1 mV/°C. In addition, the breakdown voltage, the high-frequency figure of merit, and the switching loss also improve, though the inter-electrode capacitances and the gate-to-drain charge increase. This work provides a practical solution for n-channel 4H-SiC MOSFETs adopting high-k gate dielectrics.

records.title: Impact of Mg Doping on p-GaN Gate HEMTs Fabricated by CMOS-Compatible Process
records.abstract: Tuning Mg doping is commonly used to manipulate the threshold voltage${V}_{\text {TH}}$of p-GaN gate HEMTs. However, as impurities in nature, Mg dopants might cause instabilities. In this work, by comparatively investigating four samples with Mg doping concentrations from$1.5\times 10^{{19}}$cm${}^{-{3}}$to$1.2\times 10^{{20}}$cm${}^{-{3}}$, we found that: 1) either excessively high or low Mg doping concentration will adversely affect${V}_{\text {TH}}$, 2) lower concentration of ionized holes near the Schottky junction leads to a wider depletion region in p-GaN under forward gate bias and a reduced gate leakage current, 3) severe Mg diffusion simultaneously reduces theon-state current andoff-state leakage current, 4) dynamicon-resistance degradation of devices is significantly modulated by the ionization of Mg diffused into the AlGaN/GaN, and 5) notably, although the doping concentration of$6\times 10^{{19}}$cm${}^{-{3}}$induces prominent self-compensation effects near the Schottky junction, it forms a doping level of$\sim 2\times 10^{{19}}$cm${}^{-{3}}$at the p-GaN/AlGaN heterojunction via diffusion, which occasionally achieves the maximum${V}_{\text {TH}}$. The above findings have systematically analyzed the effects of Mg doping concentration on the key electrical properties and reliability of the devices and have contributed to an in-depth understanding of the operating mechanism of p-GaN gate HEMTs.

records.title: Gate-Current-Dominated Positive Threshold Voltage Shift Under PBTI Stress in Schottky p-GaN Gate HEMTs
records.abstract: While positive bias temperature instability (PBTI)-induced threshold voltage (V${}_{\text {th}}\text {)}$instability is a major bottleneck in gallium nitride (GaN) power electronics, the role of gate current remains poorly understood and is often confounded by temperature effects. In this work, the role of gate current in threshold voltage instability is investigated using short-term PBTI stress to isolate the positive shift component before the counteracting component becomes pronounced. The positive shift decreases with increasing gate current, even at the same temperature. Moreover, nearly identical positive shifts are observed at different temperatures when the gate current is comparable. These results suggest that the positive shift is not determined by temperature alone but is associated with gate current. C–V and recovery analyses suggest that this current-dependent positive shift is associated with electron trapping. Arrhenius analysis of the secondary recovery transient of the positive shift yields an activation energy of 174 meV, suggesting trap states associated with the p-GaN/AlGaN interface.

records.title: Assessing the Effect of Solder Layer on IGBT Power Module Failures: An Evaluation Based on TSEP
records.source: Journal of Integrated Circuits and Systems
records.abstract: The Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor module (IGBT) is widely used in power electronic systems. IGBT has many advantages compared to other transistors, particularly its high voltage capacity and reduced power dissipation. Nonetheless, a challenge associated with an IGBT is its relatively high cost and its exposure to failure under high temperatures that affect its electrical characteristics, accelerating the aging failure mechanism. The solder layer reliability of the power module has been identified as the most important factor affected by junction temperature. For this reason, the thermal resistance measurement of IGBT has become a crucial part of thermal power control. Measuring the junction temperature (Tj) is essential to assess an IGBT module's degradation level. Unfortunately, obtaining accurate measurements of Tj is difficult, leading to the development of various methods intended to enhance the precision of measurements. A common method is Thermo-Sensitive Electrical Parameters, based on the measurement of a temperature-dependent electrical parameter, offering the advantage of being independent of the physical integrity of the module. The purpose of the research carried out in this paper is to estimate the solder layer damage state of an IGBT power module using experimental measurements and Scanning Electron Microscope analysis. An excellent agreement was found between experimental results and SEM analysis.

records.title: Simulation study of a split-gate superjunction SiC MOSFET with a p-type shielding layer
records.abstract: In this work, a Silicon carbide split-gate MOSFET (SGMOSFET) integrating a superjunction (SJ) structure and a P-type shielding layer (SGSJCIMOSFET) is proposed and systematically investigated using TCAD simulations. The proposed device simultaneously improves the trade-off among breakdown voltage (BV), specific on-resistance ( R ON,sp ), and switching performance. Compared with conventional VDMOSFET and SGMOSFET, the SGSJCIMOSFET achieves an enhanced BV of 3718 V and a reduced R ON,sp of 1.16 mΩ·cm 2 , resulting in an approximately 4.6× improvement in Baliga’s figure of merit. In addition, the combined effects of the split-gate and SJ structures significantly suppress the gate-to-drain capacitance to 15.2 pF cm −2 , leading to improved high-frequency (HF) performance. The incorporation of the P-type shielding layer effectively redistributes the electric field and reduces the peak oxide electric field from 4.15 MV cm −1 to 2.06 MV cm −1 . These results demonstrate that the proposed SGSJCIMOSFET is a promising candidate for next-generation high-voltage and HF power applications.

records.title: Investigation of Continuous Turn-Off Characteristics of IGBT Devices Under Overload Conditions
records.abstract: This study investigates the repetitive overload turn-off behavior of a 1200 V/15 A trench field-stop IGBT using a clamped inductive load circuit. The DC-link voltage is set to 600, 800, and 1000 V, while the external circuit configuration and the 2 ms pulse interval remain unchanged. The displayed sequences at 600 and 800 V exhibit no destructive failure. Under the 1000 V condition, 24 of 30 devices fail, and the cycle-to-failure ranges from 6 to 27. Before failure, the peak VCE, turn-off current, and Eoff reach 1248.1 V, 80.2 A, and 12.87 mJ, respectively. During the final destructive event, VCE first recovers to approximately 1.16 kV and then collapses toward zero, while IC re-grows to approximately 106.8 A. A statically validated two-dimensional simulation model shows pulse-to-pulse temperature accumulation, mobility reduction, expansion of the high-field and impact-ionization regions, and persistence of an electron-rich transport path near the trench-gate active region. Post-failure SEM reveals a filament-like damage trace, emitter-side Al damage, damaged trench-gate structures, and contiguous multi-cell ablation. The combined evidence indicates that repetitive heating progressively strengthens the coupling among carrier transport, electric-field concentration, avalanche generation, current localization, and self-heating, which leads to delayed localized electrothermal instability. An auxiliary RC-IGBT comparison further confirms that the repetitive overload turn-off boundary depends on the device technology and operating conditions.

records.title: Comparative Review of SiC and GaN Power Devices for High-Frequency DC–DC Converters
records.abstract: This structured comparative review examines silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN) wide-bandgap semiconductor (WBG) devices in high-frequency direct current (DC)-DC converters. Twenty-two peer-reviewed publications and industry reports, eleven from 2021–2026, were evaluated against criteria covering material physics, switching dynamics, converter topology performance, electromagnetic compatibility, thermal management, and reliability. A silicon-referenced normalized matrix combines material-, device-, converter-, and market-level indicators with topology mapping, electromagnetic interference (EMI) spectral comparison, and reliability physics. Reported DC-DC converter data show that GaN high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) designs reach the highest surveyed efficiency (98.5% in a 10 kW phase-shifted full-bridge above 150 kHz) and superior power density below 650 V, whereas SiC metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) devices remain preferred above 1200 V and under high thermal stress; these values are topology-specific. Parasitic inductance, conducted EMI reaching 400 MHz, and packaging remain the principal barriers to SiC MOSFET and GaN HEMT adoption in power electronics.

records.title: Simulation of enhanced short-circuit ruggedness in GaN HEMTs with a step-graded-doped p-GaN buried layer
records.abstract: This paper proposes a novel enhancement-mode gallium nitride high electron mobility transistor (GaN HEMT), featuring a step-graded doping p-GaN buried layer (TPBL-HEMT), to significantly enhance its short-circuit (SC) capability. The buried layer architecture, comprising a highly-doped source anchor, a moderately-doped main shielding region, and a lightly-doped soft termination, effectively decouples SC current suppression from electric field shaping. TCAD simulation results validate that the source anchor effectively clamps the SC current, while the soft termination modulates the drain-side electric field, thereby reducing its peak. The optimized device achieves a great SC withstand time of 1.58 µ s under a 400 V bus voltage, which is 246% longer than that of the traditional device conventional HEMT. This work presents a highly promising engineering solution for designing robust and reliable GaN power devices.

records.title: A dual-channel trench SiC MOSFET with a p-PolySi/n-SiC heterojunction tunneling channel realizing low R on,sp and V r_on
records.abstract: A novel trench 4 H-SiC MOSFET integrating an n + -PolySi/p-PolySi/n-SiC sidewall heterojunction tunneling channel , named HTC-MOS, is proposed and investigated by calibrated TCAD simulation. In the proposed HTC-MOS, one channel is realized by n + -PolySi/p-PolySi/n-SiC. Under positive gate bias, the p-PolySi interface is inverted into an electron inversion layer and the n-SiC interface accumulates a large amount of electrons, which forms an n + -PolySi/n + -SiC interface enabling significant tunneling current across the heterojunction. This tunneling-induced current path and the traditional SiC inversion channel form a dual-channel conduction path that lowers the overall channel resistance. In the reverse free-wheeling state, the p-PolySi/n-SiC heterojunction ensures lower reverse on-state voltage drop ( V R_on ) and reverse recovery charge ( Q rr ) owing to unipolar conduction. Simulation results show that the 1.2 kV rated HTC-MOS achieves an R on,sp of 1.46 mΩ·cm 2 , reduced by 24.0% compared with that of a conventional device ( R on,sp = 1.92 mΩ·cm 2 ). The V R_on is reduced from 2.96 V – 1.82 V, representing a 38.5% reduction. Q rr is reduced by 25.7%, which contributes to a 7.5% reduction in turn-on power loss.

records.title: Experimental extraction and analysis of nonlinear source resistance of GaN HEMTs
records.abstract: We conducted an experimental study on the nonlinear source resistance ( r s ) with selective n + GaN regrown Al x Ga 1 −x N/GaN high-electron mobility transistors (HEMTs). Experimental results show that r s increases with drain current, limiting current and transconductance. Using devices with different gate and access lengths, r s was extracted through a gate-current injection technique with corrected channel resistance. The effects of gate-to-source access length ( L acc-s ) and drain current on intrinsic transconductance ( g mi ) were analyzed in terms of r s . The results indicate that g mi is independent of L acc-s , confirming that the compression of g m in GaN HEMTs for high I D is primarily attributable to the nonlinear r s .

records.title: Electric-field modulation for high-voltage AlGaN/GaN HEMTs: interface engineering, field plates, and RESURF
records.source: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
records.abstract: AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) have attracted considerable attention for high-voltage power electronics owing to their high critical electric field, high electron mobility, and polarization-induced two-dimensional electron gas. However, the breakdown performance of lateral GaN HEMTs remains limited by electric-field crowding in the gate–drain access region, which produces a pronounced electric-field peak near the drain-side gate edge and promotes premature breakdown, charge trapping, and reliability degradation. Surface states and dielectric/AlGaN interface traps can further modify the field distribution and aggravate device degradation. In this context, electric-field engineering has become a central strategy for improving breakdown voltage (BV) and reliability in high-voltage GaN power devices. This review summarizes recent progress in electric-field engineering for AlGaN/GaN HEMTs, with emphasis on interface and dielectric engineering, field-plate structures, and reduced surface field-based terminations. These approaches are presented within a coordinated electric-field engineering framework, with systematic comparisons of their respective physical roles, performance benefits, design trade-offs, and practical limitations. Future directions toward the balanced optimization of BV, specific on-resistance, dynamic on-resistance, parasitic capacitance, switching performance, and long-term reliability for ultra-high-voltage GaN power devices are also highlighted.

records.title: Enhanced power performance and threshold voltage stability in quaternary InAlGaN/GaN MIS-HEMTs on Si with gate field plate
records.abstract: This work presents GaN-on-Si metal–insulator–semiconductor high-electron-mobility transistors (MIS-HEMTs) featuring a quaternary InAlGaN barrier and gate field plate (GFP) for power device applications. The proposed device has achieved a 40% increase in drain current and a 21.6% lower ON-resistance (R $$_{ON}$$ ) compared to conventional AlGaN/GaN HEMTs, due to a high carrier density of $$\sim$$ 1.9 $$\times 10^{13}\text{cm}^{-2},$$ high mobility of 1540 $$\text{cm}^{2}$$ /V·s. These enhancements yield a low specific ON-resistance (R $$_{ON,sp}$$ ) of 2.27 m $$\Omega$$ $$\cdot$$ cm $$^{2}$$ . The device also exhibits excellent breakdown performance, with a drain breakdown voltage of $$\sim$$ 950 V without Gate Field Plate (GFP) and >1500 V with GFP optimized at 4 $$\mu$$ m, enabled by a low sheet resistance (R $$_{sh}$$ ) of $$\sim$$ 215 $$\Omega$$ / $$\square$$ . Furthermore, thermal reliability is confirmed by a minimal threshold voltage (V $$_{TH}$$ ) of $$\sim$$ 0.4 V and a variation of approximately 20% in maximum drain current (I $$_{D,max}$$ ) at 150 $$^{\circ }$$ C. Moreover, this study attains a state-of-the-art achievement with a tradeoff of a high device figure-of-merit (FOM) on BV $$_{DS}^{2}$$ /R $$_{ON, sp}$$ of $$\sim$$ 1100 MW/cm $$^{2}$$ . In addition, we have also carried out the Long-term reliability under positive and negative bias temperature instability (PBTI/NBTI) stress tests under the specific bias of V $$_{GS}$$ =10 V, V $$_{DS}$$ =0 V and V $$_{GS}$$ = -30 V, V $$_{DS}$$ =0 V, respectively. It reveals that all GFP-equipped devices exhibit smaller V $$_{TH}$$ shifts under PBTI, while NBTI induces a slightly higher degradation, indicating distinct charge-trapping mechanisms in both processes.

records.title: Single and Repetitive Surge Reliability of 1200 V Asymmetric Trench SiC MOSFETs Under Various Gate Biases
records.abstract: The parameter degradation and failure mechanisms of 1200 V asymmetric trench-type (AT) silicon carbide (SiC) metal oxide semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) under various single and repetitive surge currents, with various gate bias voltages (VGS) of 0 V, −5 V, and −10 V, are systematically investigated in this work. It is indicated that VGS has no impact on the single surge reliability, with the same maximum single surge current (SSCmax) under different VGS. However, during repetitive surge stress (90% and 60% SSCmax), the maximum surge cycles have increased as VGS increases from −10 V to 0 V. It may be caused by the enhancement of channel-assisted leakage conduction, allowing more surge current to flow through the channel. It is concluded from gate capacitance (Cg-Vg) and low-frequency noise (LFN) characterizations that lower VGS increases SiC/SiO2 interface defect density, accelerating parameter degradation during single and repetitive surge stress. Both chip and package failures are observed for single and repetitive surge stress. For single surge stress, the device failure has resulted from the melted source Al as the metal erodes and penetrates through the interlayer dielectric and the ohmic contact layer between the source metal and the SiC-doped region, respectively, leading to a three-terminal short circuit. For repetitive surge stress, the device failure has been caused by the penetration of Al metal into the interlayer dielectric, leading to a gate-source short circuit. This comprehensive research provides valuable guidance for enhancing the surge reliability of SiC MOSFETs.

records.title: Prototyping a SiC JFET Drop-in Replacement Module for a 600-V, 600-A Si IGBT Half-Bridge Module
records.abstract: Silicon carbide power vertical-channel junction field effect transistors (VJFETs) are ideal candidates for next generation vehicle power systems. They combine the switching speed of MOSFETs with the voltage and current handling properties of IGBTs and the excellent thermal properties derived from the SiC material. As a unipolar device they can be easily paralleled over the entire operating range of the device and generate extremely high current for high power application. With the drop-in replacement, the case temperature of the motor drive can be significantly increased above the current limit of 80 ˚C, which will permit the designer new opportunities for decreasing size, weight, and cost. With current die area yields, the only way to fabricate high-current IPMs that can address 600-A IGBT replacement is to parallel SiC die. A process for packaging a 600-V, 600-A IGBT replacement module based on very low specific on-resistance SiC VJFETs (2.5 mΩcm2) co-packed with SiC Schottky Barrier Diodes (SBD) is reported. The design covering thermal design, material selection, and thermal (soldering) budget for the DBC and copper base plate commercial packaging is presented. The DBC design will be presented, which took into consideration accommodating 80 VJFETs in parallel and 40 SBDs in anti-parallel. All DBC were screened for single die failures using a multi-step process including high-temperature reverse bias screening. Finite element thermal analysis was utilized for appropriate packaging material selection. Successful completion of the packaging process was confirmed by DC and switching characterization.

records.title: A Design of Active Gate Driver for Reducing Surge Voltage During Turn-Off Transient of SiC MOSFET in Boost Converter
records.abstract: This paper proposes an Active Gate Driver (AGD) for a DC–DC boost converter based on Silicon Carbide (SiC) power devices, in which surge voltage and ringing arise from their fast-switching characteristics. In this work, a practical and simple 4-bit logic AGD was proposed to adjust the gate resistance during the Miller interval of the SiC MOSFET. This helps suppress these effects and lowers the surge voltage and ringing stress on the power device. Experimental results demonstrate that the voltage overshoot decreases from 52 V to 22 V, corresponding to a reduction from 52% to 22% under a 100 V output condition, while the peak drain–source voltage decreases from 152 V to 122 V. The turn-off energy increases from 60.2 µJ to 76.9 µJ due to the slightly reduced switching speed. This trade-off represents the improvement in the comparison between transient suppression and switching loss. In addition, the voltage ringing is significantly attenuated. Although the modified switching strategy slightly increases switching loss, it effectively improves waveform quality and reduces voltage stress. These results confirm that the proposed AGD provides a simple and effective solution for improving the switching robustness and reliability of SiC-based DC–DC boost converters.

records.title: Gate-Oxide Degradation in SiC MOSFETs: Common-Mode Noise as a Precursor, Theoretical Basis, and Experimental Validation
records.abstract: Gate oxide degradation is one of the dominant chip-level failure mechanisms in silicon carbide (SiC) mosfets and poses a major challenge for the long-term reliability of power electronic converters. Conventional precursors such as threshold-voltage shift, Miller plateau variation, and gate leakage current provide useful information about oxide health but typically require intrusive measurements or dedicated test intervals. This article, for the first time, investigates common-mode (CM) conducted noise as a nonintrusive, system-level precursor for gate oxide degradation in SiC mosfets. An analytical framework is first developed to link trap-induced shifts in threshold and Miller plateau voltages to changes in the switching transients and the resulting CM displacement current. The model predicts an asymmetric evolution of the drain-source voltage slopes, with a faster turn-offtransition and a slower turn-on transition as degradation progresses. These effects are shown to reshape both the time-domain CM waveform and the envelope of its frequency spectrum.The analysis in this article is validated experimentally using two discrete SiC mosfets from different manufacturers. Devices are aged by the high-electric-field-stress method, while the gate waveforms, switching transients, and CM noise are measured through a line impedance stabilization network setup. The results confirm that the CM noise amplitude and spectral content exhibit clear, monotonic trends with degradation and are consistent across both device technologies. These findings establish CM noise as a practical, nonintrusive precursor for online condition monitoring of SiC mosfet gate-oxide degradation.

records.title: Carriers transport mechanisms in p-GaN gate impacting on dynamic V TH and their novel characterization and distinction
records.source: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
records.abstract: Through a novel pulsed I – V test with an extra pre-state at sub-millisecond timescales, the effects of positive charge storage and depletion in the gate stack on the dynamic threshold voltage ( V TH ) instability are characterized and studied in a p-GaN gated enhancement-mode high electron mobility transistor. Due to the time-dependent transport behavior of carriers, the causes of negative V TH shifts have been analyzed theoretically and successfully distinguished, which are mainly attributed to the hole accumulation or hole trapping in the p-GaN gate. Moreover, distinct deviations have been revealed through the drain current transient curves under positive gate stress combined with pre-pulsed negative voltage. The detailed transport process of holes is inquired comprehensively through evaluating the temperature-dependent current transient characteristics. The traps energy levels and band offset have been given out experimentally. This study focuses on the mechanism and in-depth influence of carrier behavior on the gate performance, demonstrating that the proposed method is a powerful tool for distinguishing dynamic carrier transport processes and can help with further improvement of the dynamic instability and reliability of GaN-based HEMTs.

records.title: Physics and improvement of dynamic RON in GaN power HEMTs: A comprehensive review
records.abstract: Gallium nitride (GaN)-based high-electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) are heralding a new era in power electronics, offering high power density, fast switching speed, and high efficiency. In power switching applications, however, the performance of systems employing GaN power HEMTs is significantly impacted by dynamic on-resistance (R ON ) degradation. This phenomenon poses a critical challenge by increasing conduction loss and reducing the practical benefits of GaN technology. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the mechanisms behind dynamic R ON degradation and explores various strategies to mitigate this issue. Through a detailed analysis, the effects of buffer trapping/detrapping, surface and passivation-interface trapping, hot-electron effects under hard-switching conditions, and threshold voltage (V TH ) instability under different stress conditions are discussed, which indicates that dynamic R ON degradation arises from the coupled response of multiple trap locations and operating conditions rather than from a single trap species, with stress waveform, switching frequency, dv/dt, temperature, and thermal cycling. Furthermore, this review compares optimization techniques for dynamic R ON suppression, including buffer engineering, surface passivation, field-plate design, gate-stack stabilization, device-structure optimization, and low-thermal-budget processing. By linking physical mechanisms, characterization methods, and optimization routes, this review provides a systematic framework for understanding and reducing dynamic R ON degradation in GaN power HEMTs, paving the way for more reliable and efficient commercial power electronic systems.

records.title: Moisture-Accelerated Gate-Oxide Failure in 1200-V SiC MOSFETs Under Repetitive Avalanche Stress
records.source: IEEE Journal of Emerging and Selected Topics in Power Electronics
records.abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs are increasingly adopted in high-efficiency power systems where avalanche events are prevalent. However, the coupled impact of environmental humidity and repetitive avalanche stress is not well understood, which complicates reliability assessment under realistic mission profiles. In this work, the repetitive-avalanche characteristic lifetime to catastrophic gate-oxide breakdown is found to decrease markedly with humidity, even though the single-pulse avalanche ruggedness remains comparable at 25% RH and 85% RH; within the investigated range, the characteristic lifetime is reduced by about 15.7% for every 10% increase in RH. To clarify the underlying degradation process, fixed- and step-change-humidity UIS experiments are combined with interrupted-device EMMI, failure analysis, TCAD simulation, and capacitance – voltage (CG–VG) characterization. The results support a two-stage degradation scenario in which a localized precursor gate-leakage path first forms under repetitive avalanche with only weak humidity dependence, whereas the subsequent charge buildup and propagation to final breakdown are strongly accelerated by humidity. Based on these findings, a semi-empirical lifetime model is established to support humidity-aware repetitive-avalanche reliability assessment of the investigated 1200-V planar-gate SiC MOSFET platform.

records.title: Dynamic on-resistance degradation mechanism of 1200 V enhancement-mode GaN Schottky-gate HEMT devices on the Si substrates
records.abstract: Abstract This article reveals the dynamic characteristics of the 1200 V p-GaN high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) with Schottky-type gate contact. While 650 V GaN HEMTs have been widely adopted in practical applications, 1200 V GaN devices are still in the development stage. Although the static characteristics of 1200 V devices meet the required specifications, new challenges arise in their dynamic behavior. Specifically, when the drain voltage exceeds 600 V, a voltage tail phenomenon occurs when the drain voltage drops to around 200 V, which delays the device turn-off process. Concurrently, the dynamic on-resistance ( R ON ) of the device exhibits a resistance surge effect, increasing from 204 mΩ at 500 V to 1507 mΩ at 800 V. This degradation in dynamic resistance is primarily attributed to deep-level traps located at the Si 3 N 4 /AlGaN interface between the gate and drain region. Furthermore, the dynamic characteristics remain relatively stable with increasing temperature. According to the reverse transfer capacitance ( C rss ) results at different frequencies, the traps between the gate and drain of the device are activated, resulting in a significant increase in the switching time and dynamic R ON .

records.title: Quantification-Enabled Failure Mode Separation for IGBT Module Package Degradation Assessment
records.abstract: Insulated-gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs) are critical elements in power electronic system, and their health directly affects system reliability. Accurate degradation assessment is hindered by the strong coupling between bond-wire and solder layer degradation. This paper proposes a reliability-oriented quantitative degradation assessment method based on wear-out failure mode separation. It decouples bond-wire and solder layer effects using two diagnostic features: the on-state voltage drop at the intersection current of the IGBT I–V curve, and the on-state voltage drop at the peak current. The proposed method can independently quantify bond-wire and solder layer faults, enabling fault separation and assessment of degradation level. The relationship between the intersection current point in the hysteresis curve and the thermal response was investigated. The case study H-bridge converter demonstrates that theoretical and experimental wear-out degradation level errors of bond-wire and solder layer do not exceed 4.6% and 5.0%, respectively. The proposed method provides a quantitative wear-out degradation estimation tool for high-reliability applications, supporting online condition assessment and optimized maintenance decisions.

records.title: Characteristics of Gallium Nitride-Based Dual-Gate Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor High-Electron-Mobility Transistors with Gate Oxide Layers Directly Grown by Photoelectrochemical Oxidation Method
records.abstract: To minimize the influence of interface states and surface damage, by inserting a gate oxide layer, the photoelectrochemical oxidation method was utilized to directly grow the gate oxide layer while simultaneously creating the gate-recessed regions onto gallium nitride (GaN)-based single-gate and dual-gate metal-oxide-semiconductor high-electron-mobility transistors (MOS-HEMTs). Compared to the single-gate structure, the two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) channel layer was also modulated by the auxiliary gate, in addition to being modulated by the main gate. Consequently, a wider transconductance range, larger saturation drain-source current, lower gate leakage current, and higher drain-source breakdown voltage were the benefits derived from the auxiliary gate functionality in the dual-gate devices. Moreover, the low-frequency noise characteristics of the GaN-based MOS-HEMTs could also be improved by the dual-gate structure. These experimental results demonstrated that incorporating a dual-gate structure and directly grown gate oxide layers onto GaN-based MOS-HEMTs is a promising alternative for GaN-based low-noise, high-power, and high-frequency applications.

records.title: Development of an IGBT Dynamic–Static Test Platform and a Multi-Parameter Evaluation Method for Bridge-Arm Consistency in IGBT Modules
records.abstract: To address the need for dynamic and static parameter testing of IGBT modules, an integrated test platform was developed. In production-line applications, consistency differences in key parameters between the upper and lower bridge arms of manufactured modules were found to be difficult to quantify using a single metric. To overcome this limitation, a multi-parameter consistency evaluation method was proposed. Based on more than 400 sets of production-level measurements obtained from newly manufactured IGBT modules from the same batch, eight key parameters, including Eon, Eoff, dv/dt, di/dt, VCES, ICES, VGEth and IGES, were selected to construct paired samples of the upper and lower bridge arms. A dimensionless consistency index (CI) was introduced to quantify relative deviations between bridge arms, and consistency characteristics were analyzed using raw-parameter boxplots, CI boxplots, and paired scatter plots in terms of distribution, discrepancy quantification, and sample-wise pairing. The results show that different parameters exhibit different levels of distributional difference and relative deviation between the two bridge arms under identical test conditions, and that the three analyses reveal mutually consistent trends. The proposed method provides an effective basis for within-batch quality assessment, bridge-arm matching, abnormal sample identification, and production process troubleshooting.

records.title: Anomalous Reverse Recovery of Body Diode in 4H-SiC Superjunction DMOSFET
records.abstract: We report an anomalous reverse-recovery (RR) of the body diode in a 3.3 kV 4H-SiC superjunction (SJ) DMOSFET: at 77 K, Q RR,sp increases by 1.4×–3.5× versus room temperature and 5× versus 195 K, and J PR increases by >2×, while t RR changes by only <30ns. A clear dependence of Q RR,sp on the ramp rate at 77K indicates the Q RR,sp is not due to additional depletion charge. Current-controlled negative resistance (CCNR) is also observed solely for the SJ body diode at 77K. The voltage waveforms strongly suggest the additional Q RR,sp is due to dynamic breakdown of the SJ due to transient charge imbalance of the pillars caused by delayed hole emissions of the deep acceptors. The anomalous behavior is qualitatively reproduced in simulation. We also benchmark a 3.3kV Charge Balance (CB) 4H-SiC DMOSFET along with the SJ device from 77–423 K using an inductive double-pulse test. For T > 77 K the switching for both devices is dominated by the depletion capacitance (weak Q RR,sp dependence on the ramp rate): the SJ device turns off faster (t RR = 0.3–0.8× CB), is snappier (t B /t A = 0.23–0.56× CB), and shows larger J PR (1.8–2.8× CB) while recovering less charge (Q RR,sp = 0.4–0.8× CB). The CB device shows the expected increase of Q RR,sp with temperature and only modest t RR temperature variation. Overall, the CB device provides softer, predictable RR without a cryogenic anomaly, whereas SJ delivers the shortest t RR above 77 K but exhibits the 77 K anomalous increase and is consistently snappier.

records.title: Peak Voltage and Switching Slope Dependency of Gate Switching Instability in SiC MOSFET
records.abstract: The pursuit of ever-higher system efficiency and power density in power electronic applications paves the way for an increased utilization of wide bandgap semiconductor devices such as silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs, due to reduced conduction and switching losses compared to silicon. For real-world application reliable operation along its lifetime is of utmost importance. To assure robust operation in electric drives and traction inverters SiC MOSFETs are switched bipolar to prevent parasitic turn on. Recently, it has been shown that not only bias temperature instability, but also gate-switching instability in bipolar switched applications has to be considered as a reliability concern for SiC MOSFET. While in gate switching stress tests usually only critically damped conditions are investigated irrespective of rise and fall times, in real-world applications gate voltage overshoots may occur and a broad variety of slew rates may be used depending on the individual power converter design. Therefore, this work investigates the influence of gate voltage overshoot and voltage slopes on threshold voltage aging using high frequencies and online degradation monitoring. It is shown that overshoots have a dominating impact on the overall degradation, while the gate voltage slope impacts minorly.

records.title: IGBT Junction Temperature Prediction Model based on GA-LM-BP Algorithm
records.abstract: Aiming at the problem that the Insulated-Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT) chip is encapsulated inside the module and the chip junction temperature cannot be measured directly, an IGBT junction temperature prediction algorithm model based on the back-propagation neural network algorithm optimised jointly by the genetic algorithm and the Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm is proposed. Firstly, the temperature-sensitive electric parameter (TSEP) method is used to build an experimental platform for the saturation voltage drop of IGBT modules; then, 2250 sets of saturation voltage drop, collector current, and IGBT case temperature data are extracted from the experimental data as feature inputs to characterize their relationship with the junction temperature of the IGBT module; finally, a junction temperature prediction model is established by using the extracted electrical parameters in the Genetic Algorithm-Levenberg-Marquardt-Back Propagation (GA-LM-BP) neural network algorithm to predict the junction temperature. Finally, the GA-LM-BP neural network algorithm is used to establish a junction temperature prediction model by using the extracted electrical parameters. The experimental results show that the average absolute percentage error of the junction temperature prediction value of the GA-LM-BP neural network algorithm is 0.114 when the collector current is less than the critical current, and 0.062 when the collector current is greater than the critical current, which is more accurate than that of the GA-optimised BP neural network algorithm and classical BP neural network algorithm in predicting the junction temperature of the IGBT module.

records.title: A snapback-free RC-IGBT with low reverse-conducting voltage drop
records.abstract: The reverse conducting insulated-gate bipolar transistor (RC-IGBT) suffers from snapback phenomenon that occurs in the initial stage of forward conduction. To avoid the such phenomenon, the RC-IGBT-thyristor (TRC-IGBT) structure is used. The TRC-IGBT utilizes a p-barrier layer above the n-collector to suppress the snapback. However, with the p-barrier layer, an anti-parallel thyristor is formed when the device reverse conducts, which can cause high reverse-conducting voltage V R . In this paper, a novel TRC-IGBT is proposed to suppress the snapback phenomenon while achieving a low V R . our structure features a highly-doped N-floating layer, which is partially embedded in the p-barrier layer. The N-floating layer injects electrons into the N-base and N-buffer layer, which forms a low-resistance path connecting the N-floating layer to the p-body/N-base junction. As a result, the gate voltage of the thyristor is pulled up, which turns on the anti-parallel thyristor and a low V R is achieved. By tuning the doping concentration and width of the n-floating layer, both the forward-conducting/reverse-conducting voltage trade-off and turnoff loss/forward-conducting voltage trade-off can be optimized.

records.title: Full-Area 3D Simulation and Experimental Analysis of IGBT Failure in UIS Due to Current Filamentation
records.abstract: In spite of the importance of a detailed description of the filamentary current constriction of the IGBT during the turn-off operation that could lead to the device’s failure, there are to date no quantitative 3D simulation results of the filament growth and dynamic that can be compared with experimental results. In this paper we present 3D numerical simulations on the failure mode in the Unclamped Inductance Switching (UIS) test operation, extended to the full device area, which will be usefully compared with detailed experimental results on a large number of trench IGBT test samples. For the first time extended 3D dynamic electrothermal simulations of the whole die are made, to take into account both the electric and thermal effects of the filamentary conduction in avalanche mode. The onset of a filament growth condition for a current level just above the turnover voltage evaluated by the 3D simulations, and the area of the filament, obtained for the first time, are well in agreement with the quantitative data extracted by the experimental evaluations. Moreover, the thermal heating due to the filament formation is found to be quite independent from the current level, because it depends on the current density in the filament, rather than on the injected current. The delay time between the filament formation and the final failure time seen in the experimental results is verified to be due to the movement of the filament all around the chip surface in search of a cooler spot. The movement of the filament along the whole die area is verified for the first time by full area 3D electrothermal dynamic simulations, with times in agreement with the experimental delay between filament formation and final failure seen in all the failure reports.

records.title: Analysis of Strategies for Improving the Performance of SiC Semiconductor Devices
records.source: Transactions on Computer Science and Intelligent Systems Research
records.abstract: Due to its wide bandgap, high thermal conductivity, and high-temperature, high-frequency, and high-power characteristics, silicon carbide (SiC) has been widely applied, especially in the field of electric vehicles, power conversion and photovoltaic inverters. However, there are still some defects in the utilization of SiC-based semiconductor devices, such as lattice mismatch, material defects, and interface defects. Enhancing the stability and reliability of SiC devices themselves is an urgent issue to be solved in order to improve their performance. This study proposes four strategies to enhance the performance of SiC semiconductor devices, with a focus on improving material quality, optimizing device structure, and addressing thermal management challenges. These strategies have made significant progress in the reliability and efficiency of silicon carbide devices, especially for high-power, high-frequency applications such as electric vehicles and photovoltaic systems. Moreover, a liquid-cooled heat sink design based on topology optimization is adopted to improve the heat dissipation efficiency. Benefiting from its wide bandgap (3.26eV), high thermal conductivity (~4.9 W·cm-¹·K-¹), and strong breakdown field (~3MV/cm), SiC is inherently suited for high-temperature, high-frequency, and high-power operation. The strategies proposed in this study further leverage these advantages to enhance device performance and reliability.
